gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Redtiger's own US store sells the F17 3-channel at $129.99 today ($30 under the $159.99 B&H price ChatGPT showed), or that Redtiger names the F17's "4K" front sensor as the Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675, the same sensor Vantrue rates at 1944p on the N4S front camera.
standout_why: Compared against the cited productbible.com, dattatecblog.com and us.my-best.com pages (vortexradar.com returned 403, so it was not compared). productbible lists only one 3-channel at or under $200 (Vantrue N4S, $199.99 on Amazon, Nov 19) and has no Redtiger or Rexing. dattatecblog names the F17 3CH as its only 3-channel but gives no price, says only "STARVIS 2" and does not name the IMX675. my-best lists eight 3-channel cams with retailer prices and names no image sensor at all. None of the three gives a maker-store price for the F17 or a model-specific hardwire-kit requirement. All three give per-channel resolutions only, with nothing on which mode they apply in.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue N4S as the pick at $199.99 on vantrue.com, exactly at the budget line and linkable through awin:vantrue; ChatGPT's $179.99 BlackboxMyCar price was not re-read. It also reframes the Redtiger F17 as the budget row rather than a rival for image quality: $129.99 at Redtiger, but its 4K label sits on the sensor Vantrue rates at 1944p, its card limit is 256 GB against 1 TB, and parking mode needs a hardwire kit that is not in the box. Our existing row that fits is the Botslab G980H 4-camera at $192.70 through our link, which can run as 3 channels. The Vantrue N4 Pro S ($279.99) and Redtiger F17 Elite ($227.98 to $239.99) fall just over the line. Caveat: every Shopify store (Vantrue, Redtiger, DDPAI, Rexing) returned HTTP 429 on product pages during this run, so the Vantrue and DDPAI prices are the supplied partner-table reads of 2026-11-21, and the Redtiger figures come from its store search record, not the rendered page.
